basics.name: Dana Okonkwo
basics.label: Mechanical & Design Engineer
basics.summary: Mechanical engineer working on single-use medical devices from first sketch to tooling release; EU patent holder. Spent three years on the clean-room side of a contract manufacturer before moving into design.

work.name: Hydra Medical
highlights: Led the dose-counter redesign on an inhaler running 400,000 units a year; cut the part count from nine to five.
Built the drop and cycle test rig the team now uses for design verification, and wrote the test protocols that go with it.
Qualified two moulding suppliers, one in Portugal and one in Poland, and ran the first-article inspections.
Ran the weekly DFM reviews with the toolmaker through three rounds of T1 samples, closing 41 of 44 issues before tooling release.
Built the tolerance stack for the counter mechanism and caught a 0.3 mm interference before the first tool was cut.
Kept the design history file for the counter: 140 controlled documents through two design reviews.
Ran three rounds of formative usability testing with 14 asthma patients and changed the counter window after the second.

work.name: Polytechnic Prototyping Lab
highlights: Ran a seven-machine prototyping shop: four FDM printers, a resin printer, a benchtop mill and a laser cutter.
Taught the machine-safety induction to about 120 students a year and wrote the handbook for it.
Designed and printed over 60 jigs and fixtures for student capstone projects, from drill guides to a vacuum-forming frame.
Kept the shop’s machines running: logged and fixed about 300 faults a year, most of them within a day.
Wrote the lab’s equipment grant application: €48,000 for a five-axis mill, approved on first submission.

work.name: Self-employed
highlights: CAD and rendering for two small furniture studios, including the assembly drawings they shipped with the product.
Printed and finished 25 hinge and joint prototypes for the studios’ test assemblies.
Built a searchable parts library for one studio so their joiners could find hardware by fixing type and load.

work.name: Medisure Contract Manufacturing
highlights: Ran ISO 7 clean-room assembly for three catheter products, about 9,000 units a week across two shifts.
Cut scrap on the balloon-bonding line from 6% to 2.5% by redesigning the bonding fixture.
Set up SPC charts on the two highest-scrap stations and trained the line leads to read them.
Ran the validation build for a new catheter line: installation, operational and performance qualification on 11 stations.
Wrote or rewrote 22 work instructions after a customer audit, all accepted without findings at the follow-up.

work.name: Atelier Norte
highlights: Modelled and rendered an eight-piece outdoor furniture range for the studio’s trade-fair catalogue.

publications.name: Dose-counting mechanism for a metered inhaler

projects.name: Open-source caliper stand
highlights: Designed a printable caliper stand and published the files; about 3,000 downloads in its first year.

projects.name: Formula Student chassis jig
highlights: Designed the welding jig for the team’s steel spaceframe chassis; it held tolerance through two builds.
